title: A must-have app!
review_text:
I got to know about this app through a seminar that I was attending about credit cards. It was the most unexpected way to discover an app. I went in very sceptical because most transcription apps are absolute garbage, and specifically with a thick Indian accent, they don't tend to understand anything much, and the translation that they have is more of a work than actually typing out the entire thing.

To my surprise, this app works like an absolute masterpiece! This review currently is being transcribed through the app. I am NOT writing this for most business users, students. There are a lot of thoughts that go on in your head, but a lot of times you're not able to pen them down because you either don't have the time or your typing speed is not that great, or you lose your chain of thought while you're writing it down slowly. This app solves this problem, and the best part is it gets integrated across the entire OS, so any app that you're using, you can use Flow with it, and it does a near perfect job at transcribing everything that you have said. I very highly recommend everyone get this app. It should become a household name very very soon.

I wouldn't even be writing this review if it wasn't for the app itself. I hadn't realised what a barrier it was to productivity when I was sat down at a keyboard. I am a fairly fast typer, so that's not the issue, but I think I worry so much about ordering my thoughts that it actually becomes the problem itself to just get started. Being able to ramble on using Wispr Flow seems to reduce that barrier, and the AI orders my thoughts really nicely. I never ever leave reviews, but this seems to have made the biggest difference to me. And I have used every productivity hack or tool I can possibly find. 
I think the only feedback that I would give would be that you could add commonly used emojis into your messages (by referencing them easily). Although to be honest, I haven't actually tried that so maybe I'll give it a go.

title: Enorm gut mit noch weiterem Potenzial
review_text:
Wer an Spracherkennung in allen Apps interessiert ist, sollte diese App unbedingt ausprobieren. Da ist ganz viel bereits durchdacht, obwohl das Unternehmen noch sehr jung ist. Ich habe die Entstehungsgeschichte gelesen. Respekt! Und vielen Dank!

Die Erkennungsqualität ist faszinierend, besser gesagt: Unglaublich. Und es funktioniert nahezu in jeder App, in jedem Textfeld. Kein Kopieren mehr aus anderen Spracherkennungs-Apps. Und wer in der Lage ist, eine E-Mail in einem Zug zu diktieren, erhält sie fertig formatiert ausgegeben durch die Koppelung von Spracherkennung mit KI.

Ich würde mir allerdings wünschen, dass man Satzzeichen und Absätze auch diktieren kann. Wer das gewohnt ist, bekommt dann einfach am schnellsten und bei weniger Nacharbeit die korrekte Ausgabe. Das bekommt die KI nicht besser hin als ein schlauer Kopf.

Leider werden im Deutschen an viel zu vielen Stellen Kommas gesetzt, wo sie im Englischen hingehören, nicht aber im Deutschen. Die App ist auf Deutsch noch zu wenig angepasst. Auch geht gar nicht, dass immer wieder mit kleinen Buchstaben gestartet wird. Nomen werden aber im Deutschen nie klein geschrieben. Auch hier viel unnötige Nacharbeit leider.

Was gar nicht geht ist, dass Wörter aus nicht nachvollziehbaren Gründen einfach ersetzt werden. Wenn ich "anderswo" diktiere, möchte ich im Text nicht "andernorts" lesen. Oder dass statt eines diktierten Konjunktivs nahezu immer der Indikativ erscheint. Schließlich diktiere ich sehr bewusst.

Die Freischaltung auf iPhone ist nicht gut geregelt. Ich habe die SMS geschickt und später auch nochmals, aber eine Freischaltung ist nicht erfolgt. Irgendwie ging es dann später plötzlich doch. Und dann stelle ich fest, dass auf meinem zweiten iPhone unter dem gleichen Account dasselbe Problem wieder greift und eine Freischaltung trotz SMS-Sendung nicht erfolgt. Und SMS an eine vermutlich US-Nummer sind auch nicht gerade billig, 1 € und dann klappt es nicht einmal! Das ärgert dann.

Die größte Einschränkung bei der Nutzung stellt dar, dass man Siri bei aktiviertem Wispr Flow nur mit Tastendruck verwenden kann. Das macht die Funktionalität der App aber durchaus wett!

title: Critical Failure on iOS – Broken Permissions and Non-Existent Support
review_text:
Whisper Flow is currently completely non-functional on the latest version of iOS. The core issue is critical: the app cannot access the microphone. It fails to trigger the system-level permission prompt, and because it never requests access, it doesn’t even appear under Settings -> Privacy & Security -> Microphone. Without this, the app is essentially a digital paperweight.
I am posting this here because the official support channels are a masterclass in frustration. I’ve already submitted a request via the in-app form – which is severely limited to a tiny character count and allows no attachments or diagnostic data – but it has gone completely ignored.
The web-based support is even worse. After navigating the mandatory AI agent, the submission form becomes physically impossible to use; it won’t scroll down, meaning the "Submit" button is unreachable. It is unacceptable to charge for a product while hiding behind broken, unnavigable support walls.
Unless the developers address these basic UX and permission bugs, I strongly advise staying away. A "flow" that can’t hear its user is no flow at all.

title: It’s a relatively good app!
review_text:
Okay, I only downloaded this app because I kept getting it on ads, and I said, "Fine." Then I realized that I should have downloaded this app from the start because it's actually really helpful and it helps me whenever I don't want to type long paragraphs. My only concern is the way that the keyboard gets relatively shrunked, like it's flattened out, and the keys are flatter. That's my only concern, but this app does a really good job at what it's supposed to do, so I would say download it. I know that some people don’t want to type out anything long either, so this would be a good decision. Other than the flattening, this is a really good app! I also typed this whole paragraph just using the microphone.

Update: something that bugs me a lot is the fact I have to refresh my keyboard every time I try to type on different apps. As someone who switches between different apps for purposes, it can get a bit annoying. I know the app said they’re trying to fix it, but all I’m asking is for it to be done quicker.

This is actually pretty amazing, I'd argue better even than using voice to text on a Google Pixel device. Don't know how much pro features are going to cost but this is certainly worth paying for. Being able to keep the bubble on screen just to tap when needed is super convenient, it can even work if there's a video or something playing in the background on your device.

title: clavier qwerty?
review_text:
L'application est vraiment excellente, d'efficacité au quotidien. Certains points pourraient être améliorés, mais ne sont pas inhérents à cette application. C'est des défauts liés à des restrictions Apple, comme, depuis la mise à jour 26.4, le fait de devoir swiper entre les applications pour faire le coller.

Soit, en revanche, ce que je reproche et que j'ai du mal à expliquer, c'est que l'application utilise un clavier QWERTY, alors que, en Europe, nous sommes sur le clavier AZERTY et qu'il n'y a aucune possibilité de modifier ce réglage. Donc, si nous n'utilisons pas le mode vocal, nous sommes contraints de devoir constamment basculer entre les claviers. C'est de ma part et ça rend l'utilisation beaucoup moins agréable au quotidien.

Je mettrai à jour la vie si ce point est résolu.

When I pushed back and showed them screenshots, saying I couldn't do what they suggested, they immediately admitted that in fact there was a limitation with the software. And of course the problem that I tried to report still remains. If you have someone with an unusual name and you add their name to the dictionary, it still gets it wrong and won't allow you to attach to the misspelling multiple different mistaken interpretations of the name. So it means if it always gets the spelling wrong in multiple different ways, it only gives you the opportunity to tell it about one of the misspellings, which means that all of the other ways that it might misspell that name carry on regardless, with no opportunity to stop it from happening.

title: Personal Experience
review_text:
People used to praise Wispr Flow all across for the last few months, and I had no idea why that hype is so good, because I also use direct dictation through my Mac and iPhone, and it pretty much did the work. Yesterday, when I actually switched to Wispr Flow, I am genuinely telling you there is nothing that can be better than this. Even if you just whisper it with a very small tone, it completely analyzes every single word and gives you the result.

The main difference is actually in normal dictation, you have to cross-check whether everything was written perfectly or not, but with Wispr Flow, actually you gain the confidence. Even if you did not cross-check it, it is going to be perfectly fine, just as you spoke. 

Right now I'm doing the very same, and it has reduced my 3-hour tasks to approximately just one single hour. That too where I have to do all the grunt work of reading and analyzing instead of typing and writing.

title: Future is here!
review_text:
Fantastic app and a real game changer for writing on iPhone, Mac and PC. Czech speech recognition is surprisingly accurate — I’d estimate around 95% in my daily use. It has significantly changed how I write messages in WhatsApp, iMessage and ChatGPT.

I have three suggestions that would make it even better:

1. Improve Smart Formatting for Czech. It sometimes inserts unexpected semicolons or bullet points and doesn’t always format times (e.g. 15:30) or tennis scores (6:4, 7:5) correctly.

2. After dictation, automatically switch back to the previously used keyboard (e.g. SwiftKey). Many users use Wispr Flow only for voice input and another keyboard for manual typing. This would create a much smoother workflow.

3. The swipe gesture to start the keyboard is rather unfortunate. Hopefully Apple updates their API permissions. Having it on all the time is not the option for me - apple car play media doesn't work when Wispr flow is active.

Overall, this is one of the most impressive AI apps I’ve used recently.

I can work so much faster and get way more done because I don’t have to constantly type something, notice a typo, delete it, rewrite it, make another mistake, and then fix it again.

Now I can write around 400 words in two minutes, and there might be only two mistakes, usually with words I made up myself that the AI couldn’t possibly know. I just correct those two words and I’m done.

Something that used to take me 20–30 minutes now takes me like two or three minutes. And one of the best features is that you can actually teach the AI words you’ve created yourself, so it learns to understand them in the future.

It’s seriously a blessing and makes life so much easier, especially if you have to write a lot for work or business. By the way I installed it on every device I use or better said work with and it is amazing throughout every device (I’m using a MacBook, Windows PC and an iPhone) for business, work and private things also it is great for meeting notes while having the meeting where you can also jot down anything fast.

title: Perfect For Homeschool Planning!
review_text:
I homeschool my kids and when I have to plan their lessons I use a digital planner. A lot of the curriculum lessons have something new for every single day so it doesn't follow a pattern, which can make lesson planning very tedious and time consuming. I don't really like to just put "do lesson one, do lesson two..." because I want to know what we need to work on specifically so I can match it with activities or books or whatever we need to do, and I also like to see what we're doing ahead of time. I put in all three kids' lessons in our online planner for every curriculum and I have to do this every year. This year I was not looking forward to repeating 180 lessons or so for every curriculum for every child for every subject. So I started looking into speech-to-text and found Wispr Flow. It has made my inputting in the digital planner so much faster and convenient. I absolutely love it and it has really slashed my lesson planning timeswami down. I'm actually looking forward to lesson planning now and putting in their lessons! I don't dread it anymore! I'm going to be sad when I'm done! Ha! I love this thing -- I mostly use the desktop app on my laptop. 

I just now downloaded the phone app so I haven't really used it very much, therefore, I can't really say much about the phone app yet but the desktop app is amazing. I did discover that when using the phone app, when you hold down the space bar to move your cursor across text, the Wiser Flow keyboard it has you install and use makes that cursor fly super fast across the text when holding down the space bar. It doesn't seem to work well when holding down the space bar to move the cursor to fix stuff. And also, if you want to delete something mid sentence and start talking, it well begin with a capital letter even though you're starting in the middle of a sentence. Hopefully these minor quirks will get addressed in the future for the phone app, but it doesn't dock points off from me since my primary use is for laptop. (And when I am on my phone, I use my hold+space bar to move my cursor around text often to tighten my text or fix errors so the phone app likely won’t save time for me as much as it will on laptop. I mean, sometimes I can tap exactly where I need to fix text; but most of the time, when I tap a word to fix it, it goes to the word next to it, which is why I just hold down my space bar to move my cursor around my text. It would be nice if this weird thing was fixed on the phone app. Anyway like I said, no points taken off because I understand this is likely a personal preference.)

Thanks for building a cool tool! If you homeschool and input digital lessons, this would work great for you!!

On the iPhone, it always navigates away from the app you're in to the Wispr Flow app, and then you have to navigate back. As I understand it, that's not essentially Wispr Flow's fault. It's a restriction that Apple has put in place, but even so, it makes the experience less enjoyable than the experience on a Mac. It's just a little bit fiddly... once it's running and once it's dictating, you push the button, and it transcribes. So that'a great. review_text:
So I've experienced an issue now at least five times when making a voice note or a flow note that should be saved to scratch pad. I will say whatever it is that I need to say in the moment with the hopes of it being captured and saved. Once I finish what my voice memo or voice note actually is, there's an error with the transcription and nothing can be found. I thought the functionality allowed for the actual voice memo to at least be saved, even if the transcription wasn't, but that's not happening.

Given that a lot of my work relies on me capturing things in the moment, this is a huge issue for me. It happened once, I was okay. It happened twice, I was okay. Now this has happened five or six times, so I would like to kind of understand: what is the root cause for this? Is this normal? Is this something that's on your radar? What is the recommended fix? Because at this point it is costing me intellectual property, and that's an issue.

Wispr Flow does great if I were using it to replace my keyboard and do talk to text, but if I'm being honest, Siri can do that. I really want to see the value from Wispr Flow, which is why I decided to buy the subscription, but this has been a frustration for me.

This app has finally done it: voice to text transcription without having to fix a million things afterwards. It makes Siri look like a joke. 

Wispr flow doesn’t depend solely on understanding everything you say, like most voice to text applications. 

Wispr Flow uses AI to interpret what you intended to say, not only what it heard you say and also apply corret punctuation. 

The problem with Siri and other pure voice-to-text applications is not that they don't know how to transcribe voice to text, but that they're not always good at understanding human speech, especially when there's background noise, pauses, 1,000 different speech patterns, speeds, and accents. 

Siri isna literal interpreter. Whatever it thinks it hears is what gets transcribed. Wispr Flow applies intelligence and context. 

For example, if you say, "I need to go to the store and buy flowers for my wife for Valentine's Day," and Wispr Flow hears you say, "I need to go to the store and buy flyers for my wife for Valentine's Day," the output is going to be "flowers," not "flyers."

title: Just don’t
review_text:
If you’re thinking about getting this app, just don’t. I really thought this would be the answer to all my problems because I’m terrible at typing and I have a business so I am constantly having to write content, work on my website, answer emails and messages from clients and all that kind of stuff. I use voice dictation constantly. 

And because I have specific vocabulary for my business, the regular Apple dictation doesn’t understand what I’m saying half the time which really frustrates me. So I thought this would be the answer to my problems. Seemed good at first because I could add the words that I use to the dictionary and it would work. 

It seemed good until about the time I paid for it and then it suddenly started giving me all kinds of problems. It’s almost like a bait and switch worked great while I was on the free plan, but as soon as I ran out of minutes and had to pay to upgrade suddenly it sucked.

Multiple times I have been dictating away in a thread that was extremely important, thinking that I was doing really great and then when I go to try to send it to whatever app I’m talking to I discover that this stupid app did not capture half of what I said. 

You can’t go back and recover what you’ve just talked about for the last 15 minutes so you just wasted your time and by that point you’re so mad that you don’t even want to start over again.

My time is entirely too valuable to be wasting on an unreliable app that can’t decide if it wants to stay awake and pay attention to what I’m saying or not.

I am only happy that I only paid for one month instead of a year like I was considering doing. Now I just have to wait till the month is over and it’s $15. I can’t get back. I’ll probably continue to experiment with it until the month is up to see if it gets any better but I’m not going to use it for anything really important because it’s too frustrating to lose your progress and I don’t really need to use it for things that aren’t important so I don’t really know what the point of this app even is.

title: Uninstalled in 5minutes

Used it for just 5 minutes, and honestly, the dictation is nowhere near good enough.

If this is supposed to be AI-based, the AI still feels very immature. It keeps getting basic words wrong. In just 5 minutes, it made around 10 mistakes, which is a lot for something that is supposed to accurately understand speech.

Guys, just compare its dictation with ChatGPT. You’ll immediately understand the difference. ChatGPT’s dictation is far more accurate and works smoothly with almost no noticeable mistakes.

I don’t understand why the AI is still struggling so much with basic speech recognition. If the Whisper AI is mainly learning from an individual user’s speaking patterns, I honestly don’t think that’s the right approach. It should be trained on broader speech patterns and data from a much larger and more diverse user base.

The potential is there, but right now the dictation needs a LOT of improvement. ChatGPT is clearly ahead in this area.

title: Great when it works, but far too unreliable
review_text:
As someone with dyslexia, Wispr Flow seemed like the perfect app. Unfortunately, I’ve experienced so many problems that it has become practically useless.

* Account syncing: I signed up on my computer, but my plan hasn’t carried across to my phone—even though I’m using the same account. Perhaps I’ve missed something, but it shouldn’t be this difficult.
* Lost dictation: Sometimes the app simply doesn’t work, with no warning. You can speak for quite a while before it reports a problem and loses everything you’ve just dictated. Dictation isn’t quicker if you then have to rewrite the entire thing.
* Awkward to use: The experience isn’t seamless. I regularly have to open the Wispr Flow app and then return to whichever app I was using before I can start dictating again. It feels clunky and wastes time.
* Terrible keyboard: The keyboard frequently mistypes words and misses letters. It looks similar to Apple’s keyboard, but performs far worse. You’re almost forced to use dictation even when you only want to type something quickly. There’s no emoji button either, so you have to keep switching keyboards.

When Wispr Flow works, it’s great. Unfortunately, the number of times it fails is infuriating, and the keyboard is awful. I couldn’t even write this review using Wispr Flow.

My phone and the app are both fully up to date. Considering how much the subscription costs, it simply isn’t worth the hassle. Save your money and use your phone’s built-in dictation—it’s nearly as good, much easier to use, and far more reliable.

It will paste into nothing, and you will have to go to the program and get the history information again. 🏆 RATING IMMÉDIAT — Spokenly gagne, et pas de peu

Critère	Wispr Flow	Spokenly
Homophones ver/verre/vers/verte	0/4 — « vert » partout	4/4 ✅
Chiffres	2 erreurs graves	0 erreur ✅
Mots rares (7)	2/7	5/7
Argot (4)	0/4	3/4
Toponymes	Salange, Saxonnet ❌	Sallanches ✅, Saxonex ~
Grammaire	cassée (« sera distingué »)	intacte ✅
Typographie	plate	apostrophes courbes, accents, tirets insécables ✅
Total erreurs	20	7
Score	48 %	85 %

Et le coup de grâce : Spokenly a fait ça avec un dictionnaire VIDE. Wispr Flow tournait avec le sien, rodé. L'écart réel est donc plus large que le tableau.

Les 2 erreurs qui disqualifient Wispr Flow

	•	« Je pèse 89,9 kg » au lieu de 99,9. 10 kg d'écart.
	•	« Je mesure 1 m, soit 117 » — bouillie.

title: iOS handing off issues
review_text:
I’ve subscribed to Wispr Flow for almost a year, and there is one persistent iPhone issue that is probably going to keep me from renewing.

I regularly use AirPods with both my iPad and iPhone and switch back and forth between the two devices throughout the day. When my AirPods have been in use with my iPad and I then try to start Wispr Flow on my iPhone, Flow often becomes extremely unreliable.

I’ll press Start Wispr Flow, it switches into the Flow app and then sends me back to the app I was typing in, but dictation hasn’t actually started. I then have to press Start again and go through the same app-switching process two or three times. Other times the Flow microphone becomes completely grayed out and I can’t start it at all. Sometimes I have to manually open Flow, force-quit it, reopen it, and then return to the app where I was trying to dictate.

I’ve also tried setting Flow to use the iPhone’s built-in microphone rather than the AirPods microphone. That does not solve the problem. The issue appears to be triggered simply by the AirPods being connected and switching between my Apple devices, rather than by which microphone Flow is actually using.

The only reliable way I’ve found to prevent it is to open Control Center on my iPhone, manually change the audio output to the iPhone speaker, and then start Flow. That works, but having to perform an extra audio-routing step every time defeats much of the convenience of a voice-dictation app.

After nearly a year of using the service, I would have expected the interaction between Flow, iOS, and AirPods to be much more reliable by now. If this still hasn’t been resolved after this long, I don’t have much confidence that it will be, and at this point I don’t see much reason to renew my subscription.

A dictation app needs to make speaking into my phone faster and easier, not turn starting dictation into a 20-second troubleshooting process

title: The beat until you don’t need it
review_text:
I hate to post this review. I've consistently, for a year-plus, been a top 1% user of Wispr Flow according to their monthly review, I've seen posts from people talking about getting things right. Unfortunately, it feels like another app that's great while using it, but only until it gets replaced. It doesn't need to be that way, but it's the engineering.

I'm finding so many day-to-day frustrations when you're on the Wispr Flow keyboard and you exit or aren't using voice. You end up with two keyboards overlaid, which is a very poor UI bug that has been unaddressed for at least a month. Seems like it was 3 to 6 months ago that they got rid of swipe keyboard functions altogether. Not sure if that was something that was sprung on them by Apple. If so, I have sympathy.

Anytime I want to swipe, which is anytime I want to write on the keyboard directly, I have to switch from their keyboard to Apple's. Tonight, I was trying to use their Notepad quick-note function. I dictated twice, and my iPhone screen either timed out and shut off or I closed it, but it didn't ever stop recording. It picked up absolutely nothing.

After a few sessions of talking about very important things, I ended up capturing none of it and realized I would never trust that again. 

I do like having one app across multiple platforms to capture all my text, but increasingly, I'm realizing that Wispr Flow will last only until I have a sufficient voice-to-text alternative. At the very least, ChatGPT has arrived. So even if I had to go to the ChatGPT app to do transcripts, I could do that and would no longer need this app. It's still copy-paste, but would not have the gaps, which would be nice not to have anymore.

title: 5-Star Review: Wispr Flow is the Best Voice-to-Text App I’ve Used
review_text:
I really enjoy using Wispr Flow—it’s a top-quality app that does an excellent job converting dictation into concise, grammatically correct, and professional messages. The overall experience is impressive, and it’s clear a lot of thought has gone into making it powerful and user-friendly.

That said, there are a couple of areas that could use more attention. Every update continues to use the same vague text. Even the current one says, “We’ve tuned up Flow to make it smoother than ever so you can stop typing – start speaking,” but it doesn’t explain what was actually improved. More detailed release notes about bug fixes, new features, and ways the app distinguishes itself from competitors would be very helpful.

There is also a persistent iOS issue they previously said they would address but have not updated us on. When driving or listening to music, if I try to dictate a text using Flow, the music playing through Apple CarPlay suddenly switches to my iPhone at full volume. This is distracting, can affect the accuracy of dictation, and when finished, the audio sometimes abruptly returns to CarPlay, which is jarring. This makes using Flow in real-world scenarios like driving challenging and potentially unsafe.

Given the subscription prices it would be great to see more detailed updates and timely fixes for issues like this. These points are just a few things to highlight, and overall, I continue to really enjoy using Wispr Flow.

As a suggestion for future development, it would be incredibly useful to have an Apple CarPlay app that allows me to activate Wispr Flow directly from the CarPlay interface and dictate messages as well as a Siri extension —whether to iMessage or other messaging apps—safely while driving or not driving. This would make the app even more powerful and convenient for real-world use. Thank you for a wonderful App.

title: Bug bei Korrektur des letzten Worts im Satz
review_text:
Tolle App, viele Möglichkeiten der Konfiguration. Aber es gibt einen sehr nervigen Bug: wenn ich das letzte Wort in einem Satz, also vor dem Punkt, korrigiere, wird die deutsche Sprache nicht mehr akzeptiert. Die App schreibt das Wort in irgendein beliebiges englisches Wort um. Es ist dann nicht mehr möglich, das Wort in Deutsch zu schreiben. Es wird immer verändert. Auch wenn Deutsch als Standardsprache eingestellt ist.
Eine andere Sache: der Cursor ist viel zu schnell, wenn man die Space Taste benutzt. Viel schneller als mit dem Standard Tastatur Layout. Das macht eine Steuerung schwierig bis unmöglich.
